chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Sufyan ibn Salih and Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from al-Halabi, from Hisham ibn Salim Salim and 'Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Muskan, all of them, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him):

He (peace be upon him) was asked about walnuts, when one cannot count them, so they are measured by a measure, then what is in it is counted, then what remains is measured according to that count. He said, 'There is no objection to it.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no objection / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: How to calculate the price of bulk goods when exact counting is difficult in Islamic trade?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates a practical method for resolving *gharar* in bulk commodity trade by using a counted sample to establish a reliable ratio for the remainder. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle of facilitating commerce by allowing proportional estimation when exact counting is burdensome, provided the method ensures fairness and minimizes dispute. It underscores the flexibility of fiqh in addressing real-world economic challenges while maintaining contractual integrity.
